newsitem.title: USA: Mass. to challenge Prudential fraud settlement.
newsitem.headline: Mass. to challenge Prudential fraud settlement.

text.p: Massachusetts will urge a federal judge Thursday to reject a proposed $410 milllion settlement of life insurance sales fraud charges against Prudential Insurance Co of America, the state's insurance commissioner's office said.

U.S. District Court Alfred Wolin of the New Jersey district gave his preliminary approval in October to the proposed payment of at least $410 million to as many as 10.7 million Prudential policyholders to settle improper sales practice claims.
Spokeswoman Lisa Birknes of the state insurance agency said the brief will be filed Thursday in conjunction with the Mass. attorney general's office.

Massachusetts is among a handful of states which have not agreed to the proposed settlement. Joanna Connolly, an assistant attorney general for Massachusetts, told Reuters that Florida and Texas would also file with the court their opposition to the plan. "We don't think (the settlement) goes far enough, so we sent down our objections," Connolly said. "We like the idea of a settlement, but you've got to make it more consumer friendly."
The recent disclosure that a Prudential employee destroyed documents crucial to the case heightened the state's desire to take a tough line, Connolly said.
On Monday, Prudential said it fired John Breedlove, managing director of its Cambridge, Mass., office, for destroying documents which could be relevant to the case.

"If we find that Prudential agents have been doing the wholesale destruction of documents, that makes it even more important that the consumers do not have the whole burden of proof" to prove they were wronged, Connolly said.

Connolly said the Massachusetts attorney general's office will investigate the alleged document destroying at the Cambridge agents office. She said initially the investigation will focus on that particular office, but it could be expanded.

A hearing on the fairness of the proposed settlement is scheduled for January 21. Prudential earlier this year agreed to pay a record $35 million fine and reimburse customers nationwide as part of a separate multi-state settlement.
